newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait gives go ahead to steel venture with Iran.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait gives go ahead to steel venture with Iran.

text.p: Kuwait has authorised the building of a steel reinforced bar mill in a $70 million joint venture project with Iran, officials said on Wednesday.

"We have issued approvals for three steel projects, including one involving Kuwaiti, Gulf Arab and Iranian investors," the head of the Kuwait General Industry Authority, Nasser al-Ojail, told Reuters.

The National Iranian Steel Company (Nisco) will have a 49 percent stake in the proposed mill which is expected to produce about 300,000 tonnes a year. Mainly private Kuwaiti investors will hold the rest.
Kuwait's annual use is estimated at 400,000 tonnes.
The Austria-based Voest-Alpine Industrieanlagenbau appears to be the front-runner for a contract to supply and install the new mill's equipment, industry sources said on Wednesday.
"I think there is still one other company, an Italian firm, on the short list," one source said without elaborating. "Nothing has been signed yet with Voest."
The project, which will import production materials mainly from Iran, could take under two years to complete.

One of the other two projects approved will use material from Saudi Arabia to produce 128,887 tonnes of steel a year and the second will use scrap to produce steel bars with an annual capacity of 50,000 tonnes.
